title: Luyện Đọc VSTEP: The History of Writing Systems (VstepR2-Test 15 (27-03-2026))

tasks.instructions: Directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.

passage.title: The History of Writing Systems
passage.text:
Writing is one of humanity's most transformative inventions, enabling the accumulation and transmission of knowledge across generations. The earliest known writing system, cuneiform, was developed by the Sumerians of Mesopotamia around 3200 BCE. Initially used for bookkeeping and administrative records, it consisted of wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay tablets. Over centuries, cuneiform evolved to represent syllables and words and was adapted by many subsequent civilizations, including the Akkadians, Babylonians, and Assyrians.

Independently, the ancient Egyptians developed hieroglyphics — a system combining logographic, syllabic, and alphabetic elements — around 3100 BCE. Hieroglyphics were used primarily for religious and monumental inscriptions and were carved into stone or painted on papyrus scrolls. A simpler cursive form, known as hieratic script, was developed for everyday use. The Rosetta Stone, discovered in 1799 and inscribed with the same decree in Greek, hieroglyphic, and demotic scripts, was the key that allowed scholars to finally decipher Egyptian hieroglyphics in the 19th century.

The most widely used writing system today — the Latin alphabet — has its roots in the Phoenician alphabet, developed around 1050 BCE. The Phoenicians were seafaring merchants who needed a simple, portable script for commerce. Their 22-character consonant-based alphabet was adopted and modified by the ancient Greeks, who added vowels, creating the basis for Latin and eventually most modern Western scripts. Today, the Latin alphabet is used by approximately 70% of the world's population and forms the foundation of hundreds of languages.
